 Hon'Ble Sameer Jain, J. 
1.

Sri Jadu Nandan Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri R.N. Srivastava, learned Aga
for the State-respondent are present.

2. The instant transfer application has been filed by the applicant with a prayer to transfer case No.
162 of 2020 arising out of case crime No. 375 of 2019, u/s 498A, 323, 506 Ipc & Section 3/4 Dowry
Prohibition Act, P.S. Kotwali Chhibramau, District Kannauj, pending in the Court of Additional
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chhibramau, Kannauj to the court of competent jurisdiction in District
Farrukhabad.

3.  At the very outset, learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is father in law of the opposite party no. 2 and he filed instant transfer application with a prayer to transfer the trial of the case relates to offence under section 498 A IPC from District Kannauj to District Farrukhabad but applicant is ready to appear through video conferencing and therefore, the instant application may be disposed off with the direction that if applicant filed an application before appropriate forum to appear through video conferencing then his application shall be entertained and he will be permitted to appear through video conferencing.
4. Learned AGA is having no objection.

5. The instant transfer application has been filed by the applicant who is father in law of the opposite party no. 2 with a prayer to transfer the case from District Kannauj to District Farrukhabad but now he is ready to pursue the matter through video conferencing, therefore, instant transfer application is disposed off with a direction that if applicant filed an application to pursue through video conferencing then his application shall be considered and he will be permitted to pursue the matter through video conferencing.
(Sameer Jain,J.) November 6, 2025 Ankita  Havaldar Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39315153/
